# gCanvas

This fork refactors elementalDraw into one responsibility: a 2D canvas API with interchangeable
OpenGL and Vulkan renderers. It is a rendering dependency for Flex, not a second widget, layout,
or application framework.

The current `0.8` boundary contains:

- `gCanvas::Core`: backend-neutral canvas, color, font, image, and geometry contracts.
- `gCanvas::OpenGL`: the OpenGL renderer.
- `gCanvas::Vulkan`: the Vulkan renderer.
- `gCanvas::Window`: an optional GLFW presentation helper with runtime backend selection.
- `gCanvas::gCanvas`: a convenience aggregate of the enabled targets.

The UI, audio, video, ThorVG, and experimental Metal branches from upstream were removed from the
vendored fork. NanoGUI remains an integration helper; it is not a gCanvas backend.

## Build

The manifest uses vcpkg for GLFW, FreeType, stb, glad, Vulkan headers/loader, Vulkan Memory
Allocator, and Vulkan utility libraries. Vulkan validation layers and diagnostic tools remain
optional developer packages.

```powershell
cmake -S . -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64 `
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=C:/tools/vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake `
  -DGCANVAS_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build --config Release
ctest --test-dir build -C Release --output-on-failure
```

The standalone build also creates `gcanvas_showcase` by default. It is a resize-aware animated
scene covering gradients, SVG paths, analytic outer shadows, affine transforms, stencil clipping,
and translucent text and images on the same runtime-selected canvas contract:

```powershell
build/Release/gcanvas_showcase.exe opengl
build/Release/gcanvas_showcase.exe vulkan
```

Pass `--smoke` to render two hidden frames and exit; this is also registered in CTest for every
enabled backend.

Use `GCANVAS_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF` for library-only builds. When gCanvas is included as a subproject,
examples remain off unless explicitly requested.

The Vulkan fragment shader has a checked-in GLSL source and generated byte include. Normal builds
consume the generated include and therefore do not require a shader compiler. After editing the
shader, regenerate it with `glslangValidator` from the Vulkan SDK or the vcpkg
`glslang[tools]` feature:

```powershell
cmake -DGLSLANG_VALIDATOR=C:/path/to/glslangValidator.exe `
  -DSHADER=src/shaders/rounded_rect.frag `
  -DOUTPUT=src/shaders/rounded_rect.frag.spv.inc `
  -P cmake/GenerateSpirvInclude.cmake
```

Each renderer can be selected independently with `GCANVAS_BUILD_OPENGL` and
`GCANVAS_BUILD_VULKAN`. `GCANVAS_BUILD_WINDOW` links the enabled renderer set. Requesting a backend
that was not built is an explicit initialization error; gCanvas never substitutes another
renderer.

OpenGL also supports an external presentation mode for embedding into an existing renderer. The
host keeps its context current and swaps buffers; gCanvas owns only its draw resources and requires
procedure-loading plus framebuffer-size callbacks. `present_frame()` remains mandatory because it
releases per-frame command pins even though it does not swap in this mode.

## Runtime selection

```cpp
#include <gcanvas/window.hpp>

int main()
{
    gcanvas::WindowConfig config{"Canvas", 800, 600};
    config.backend = gcanvas::Backend::Vulkan; // or gcanvas::Backend::OpenGL

    auto window = gcanvas::Window::create(config);
    gcanvas::Context& canvas = window->create_context();
    canvas.set_clear_color(gcanvas::color("#101820"));

    while (window->is_running())
    {
        window->poll_events();
        canvas.set_fill_color(gcanvas::color("#f2aa4c"));
        canvas.fill_rounded_rect(24, 24, 220, 72, 12);
        canvas.draw_frame();
        canvas.present_frame();
    }
}
```

Images and fonts are backend-specific resources and must be created through their canvas:

```cpp
gcanvas::Image& logo = canvas.create_image("logo.png");
gcanvas::Font& body = canvas.create_font("body.ttf");
canvas.set_font(body);
```

The context owns these resources. Their references remain valid until context teardown; there is
no public `destroy()` operation. Input image/font buffers are copied during creation. Calling
`Image::update_data()` updates the retained pixels and synchronously uploads them through the
creating backend.

Memory-backed images require an explicit byte length so the canvas can reject truncated spans:

```cpp
gcanvas::Image& icon = canvas.create_image(width, height, 4, rgba.data(), rgba.size());
```

For direct construction, include `<gcanvas/backends/opengl.hpp>` or
`<gcanvas/backends/vulkan.hpp>`. Those typed factories return `std::unique_ptr<gcanvas::Context>` and
take copied create-info records containing canvas metrics, resource limits, and borrowed host
callbacks. Renderer targets do not include or link GLFW; the optional `Window` target adapts GLFW
to those callbacks. The exact lifetime and frame rules are normative in
[docs/host-and-resource-protocol.md](docs/host-and-resource-protocol.md).

## Compatibility

Upstream static factories `Context::create`, `Image::create`, and `Font::create` are intentionally
removed. Backend choice is no longer a compile-time macro. Existing drawing operations keep their
names and behavior, while operations that only printed “not implemented” are not exposed as public
API.

## Paths and paints

`Path`, `Paint`, and `Transform` are backend-neutral values. Both GPU backends consume the same
bounded tessellated geometry, so path and paint semantics do not diverge by API:

```cpp
gcanvas::Path path;
path.move_to(20, 80).cubic_to(60, 10, 140, 10, 180, 80).line_to(20, 80).close();

auto paint = gcanvas::Paint::linear_gradient(
    20, 0, 180, 0,
    {{0.0f, gcanvas::color("#ff4d4d")},
     {0.5f, gcanvas::color("#4dff88")},
     {1.0f, gcanvas::color("#4d70ff")}});

canvas.fill_path(path, paint, gcanvas::Transform::rotation(0.1f));
canvas.stroke_path(path, gcanvas::Paint::solid(gcanvas::color("#ffffff")), 2.0f);
```

Paths provide lines, quadratic/cubic Beziers, rectangles, rounded rectangles, and ellipses.
`Path::from_svg()` accepts absolute or relative `M/L/H/V/C/Q/A/Z` commands and rejects unsupported
or malformed input. Paints provide solid color, multi-stop linear/radial gradients, and borrowed
context-owned image patterns. Affine path, text, complete-image transforms, and convex clipping are
supported through the shared `Transform` contract. Axis-aligned rectangles retain the scissor fast
path; transformed and intersected clips use a convex stencil mask.
Fill/stroke coverage, monochrome and color glyphs, and tinted images all use straight-alpha
composition consistently in OpenGL and Vulkan.

Primitive outer shadows use the current fill color. Their bounds remain the fully opaque shape;
the final argument is a non-negative blur radius in logical canvas units, and coverage expands
outwards instead of shrinking the source shape:

```cpp
canvas.set_fill_color(gcanvas::color(0, 0, 0, 96));
canvas.draw_rounded_rect_shadow(28.0f, 34.0f, 220.0f, 96.0f, 16.0f, 12.0f);
canvas.set_fill_color(gcanvas::color("#253451"));
canvas.fill_rounded_rect(28.0f, 34.0f, 220.0f, 96.0f, 16.0f);
```

The same shader-space distance field drives rectangle, rounded-rectangle, and circle shadows in
both GPU backends. Invalid bounds, radii, or blur values fail before a draw record is queued.

Arbitrary paths, glyphs, and image alpha can use the shared sampled outer-shadow API. The core
builds one deterministic, bounded kernel; path samples remain tessellated stencil draws, while
text and images use their existing GPU alpha textures in silhouette mode. No source pixels are
read back and no temporary framebuffer is allocated:

```cpp
canvas.set_fill_color(gcanvas::color(0, 0, 0, 128));
canvas.draw_path_shadow(path, 0.0f, 8.0f, 2.0f, transform);
canvas.draw_text_shadow(20.0f, 40.0f, "shadow", 6.0f, 1.0f, transform);
canvas.draw_image_shadow(20.0f, 60.0f, 64.0f, 32.0f, logo, 6.0f, 1.0f, transform);
```

Source-color blur uses the same deterministic Gaussian kernel while preserving the path paint,
glyph color, or image pixels. It is a draw-state operation rather than a whole-frame postprocess:
each call emits an ordered group of GPU commands, remains subject to the active clip, and does not
sample content drawn before it. A zero radius is source-equivalent; invalid radii fail before any
blur command is queued.

```cpp
canvas.draw_path_blur(path, paint, 0.0f, 6.0f, transform);
canvas.draw_text_blur(20.0f, 40.0f, "blur", 6.0f, transform);
canvas.set_fill_color(gcanvas::color(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 0.8f));
canvas.draw_image_blur(20.0f, 60.0f, 64.0f, 32.0f, logo, 6.0f, transform);
```

Path blur tessellates once and acquires at most one existing transient paint texture, then reuses
that geometry and texture across every tap. Text and image blur reuse their atlas/source texture.
There are no blur-owned framebuffers, descriptor sets, image layouts, or resize-time resources.
The context owns the frame command vectors; they transition from empty to recording to consumed
and are cleared by the existing frame lifecycle. `max_blur_samples` (25 by default) and
`max_blur_commands` (65,536 per path call) are checked before vector reservation or texture
acquisition. Thus a path blur has `O(Q * S)` command memory, where
`(Q + 1) * S <= max_blur_commands`; allocation failure leaves that blur call unqueued.
The backend command vectors keep their bounded frame high-water capacity and grow geometrically
instead of reallocating for every blurred path. This preserves the preflight allocation guarantee
while avoiding repeated command-buffer copies during a larger frame.

`draw_*_inset_shadow` provides analytic rectangle, rounded-rectangle, circle, and ellipse inset
coverage. Arbitrary paths use the original and shifted stencil coverage, while text and images
sample their existing alpha textures. All inset variants are submitted after the source content,
do not allocate a temporary framebuffer, and remain clipped by the active canvas mask. Signed
spread is supported throughout: sampled paths use bounded stencil dilation/erosion geometry,
while glyph and image alpha use a fixed 5x5 disk GPU morphology kernel (13 active taps). Negative outer spread erodes
the source mask; negative inset spread dilates the shifted mask.

```cpp
canvas.set_fill_color(gcanvas::color(32, 48, 80, 160));
canvas.draw_path_inset_shadow(path, 0.0f, 4.0f, 2.0f, 6.0f, 1.0f, transform);
canvas.draw_text_inset_shadow(20.0f, 40.0f, "inset", 3.0f, 0.0f,
                              4.0f, 0.0f, transform);
canvas.draw_image_inset_shadow(20.0f, 60.0f, 64.0f, 32.0f, logo,
                               3.0f, 0.0f, 4.0f, 0.0f, transform);
```

```cpp
const auto image_transform = gcanvas::Transform::translation(120.0f, 40.0f) *
                             gcanvas::Transform::rotation(0.25f);
canvas.draw_image(0.0f, 0.0f, 64.0f, 32.0f, logo, image_transform, true);
canvas.draw_text(0.0f, 48.0f, "affine text", image_transform);
canvas.set_convex_mask({{20.0f, 8.0f}, {48.0f, 20.0f},
                        {36.0f, 48.0f}, {8.0f, 36.0f}});
```

The shared tessellator adaptively flattens cubic curves into bounded triangle/quad geometry.
OpenGL and Vulkan reserve independent stencil bits for path coverage, shifted inset coverage, and
convex clipping, so path cleanup preserves an active transformed clip. Solid paints allocate no texture and opaque image patterns reuse
their source GPU image directly. Gradients and translucent image patterns reuse fixed
`path_paint_texture_size` square lookup textures rather than uploading a full-canvas RGBA surface.
`max_path_mesh_quads`, `max_clip_vertices`, `max_path_surfaces`, `max_shadow_samples`,
`max_blur_samples`, and `max_blur_commands` bound geometry, clipping, transient paint resources,
sampled shadow work, and source-color blur work;
exceeding either limit fails immediately.

The sampled path command cost is `O(Q * S)`, where `Q` is the bounded tessellated quad count and
`S <= max_shadow_samples` (25 by default). Signed-spread texture shadows remain `O(S)` draw
records and use 13 bounded alpha lookups per fragment. These correctness paths introduce
no per-frame framebuffer or GPU allocation.

This is backend-native GPU rasterization, not hardware tessellation-shader subdivision: curve
flattening remains shared CPU work so OpenGL and Vulkan have one geometry fact source. GPU stencil,
coverage rasterization, blending, and texture sampling own the pixel stage. OpenGL hosts must
provide at least three stencil bits; the GLFW helper requests eight. Vulkan creates a per-swapchain
depth/stencil attachment and fails if the device exposes no supported stencil format.

The vendored NanoVG implementation in `vendor/nanovg/nanovg` remains a behavioral and algorithmic
reference. NanoVG types do not cross the public boundary, and OpenGL/Vulkan must pass the same
contract and pixel tests. Any source adapted from NanoVG must retain its origin and license notice.

Upstream source: <https://github.com/Haeri/elementalDraw>, forked from commit
`ae5ffa762d2708267f16a8671daa7b010cfbbc25`. The upstream MIT license remains in `LICENSE`.
